thread:
customer-john: Hey @support — prod private deployment (vpc-prod-2a) started failing to reach Redwood control plane ~09:12 UTC. All inference requests time out, TLS handshake never completes. We rolled back canary, no change.

customer-john: curl shows handshake timeout: 
```
$ curl -v https://control.redwood.example.com/ping 
* About to connect() to control.redwood.example.com port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 54.123.45.67...
* connect to 54.123.45.67 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to control.redwood.example.com port 443: Connection timed out
```

support-ian: Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the data. A couple quick Qs: are the affected hosts in a private subnet using a NAT gateway? Any recent SG/NACL changes? Also, can you share the SG and NACL for the subnet and the route table?

customer-john: We use private subnets with a NAT gateway in the public subnet (nat-0a1b2c). No route changes. We did update outbound SG rules yesterday to be more restrictive (security team tightened it down). SG attached to nodes: `sg-0node` inbound: 1024-65535 TCP from alb, outbound: 0.0.0.0/0:443 allowed only. NACL for subnet is custom: inbound allows 443 from 54.123.45.0/24, outbound allows 443 to 54.123.45.0/24, deny all else.

maya: That NACL config looks suspicious — remember NACLs are stateless. If SG allows outbound 443 but NACL only allows outbound 443, the ephemeral port range for return traffic may be blocked. For TCP the client uses ephemeral source ports (eg 32768) and the control plane responds back to those. With a stateless NACL you need to allow the ephemeral range in the inbound/outbound directions as appropriate.

sam-engineer: Quick repro steps I used locally:
```
# from a node in the subnet
$ nc -vz control.redwood.example.com 443
Connection timed out
# add a temporary iptables DNAT to test via NAT gateway, works -> indicates egress path issue
```

support-ian: Two common fixes:
- Update the subnet NACL to allow ephemeral port range 1024-65535 for inbound (source 54.123.45.0/24) and outbound (destination 54.123.45.0/24).
- Or relax outbound SG to 0.0.0.0/0:443 and ensure NAT gateway route works (but NACL still needs ephemeral ports allowed for return).

customer-john: So we need both directions? We currently have inbound NACL allow 443 from control plane range but not ephemeral. Example NACL rules we have:
```
Rule 100 ALLOW TCP 443 54.123.45.0/24 (ingress)
Rule 110 ALLOW TCP 443 54.123.45.0/24 (egress)
Rule * DENY ALL * *
```

maya: Yeah that will fail. You should add rules like:
```
# allow established return traffic (ephemeral ports)
Rule 120 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 54.123.45.0/24 (ingress)
Rule 121 ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 54.123.45.0/24 (egress)
```
NACLs are evaluated by rule number; ensure ephemeral rules evaluate before the deny.

support-ian: Also check TLS/ALPN if you have an outbound proxy. If using AWS NAT Gateway the source IP will be the NAT's elastic ip, so your NACL/source CIDR checks should account for that (eg allow ephemeral ports for 52.34.XX.XX/32 if that's your NAT EIP).

customer-john: Ah — our security team allowed only 54.123.45.0/24 in the NACL but the NAT EIP is 52.34.210.12. So return packets from control plane go to the NAT IP but the NACL denies ephemeral.

sam-engineer: For immediate mitigation you can:
1) Add ephemeral range allow rules to the NACL and make sure rule number < 32768 deny.
2) Or put the worker subnet in a different NACL that is more permissive.

infra-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-0042 — "control-plane egress failure from prod private subnet" — assigned to network-team.

support-ian: Once you update NACL rules, confirm with `curl -v` and `traceroute -p tcp control.redwood.example.com 443` from a node. If you want, paste the NACL rule table here and we can eyeball it. :thumbsup: 

customer-john: Thanks team, changing rules now. Will report back in ~10m with results.

support-ian: If it persists after ephemeral rules are added, also verify SG stateful behavior (SGs are stateful so usually fine) and check any host firewall (iptables) blocking high ports.

customer-john: Update — after adding ephemeral allow rules and accounting for NAT EIP, requests succeed again. TLS handshake completes and inference latency is normal. Thanks for the quick help! :party-parrot:
